text: Given an input referring expression specifying fine-grained contextual attributes...
...along with an input query image containing target objects,
the backbone and feature enhancer extract cross-modality representations.
This yields multi-scale cross-modality visual feature maps across four resolution levels.
A linear projection layer maps the visual features into the text embedding space.
Simultaneously, the extracted text feature vectors are prepared.
The corresponding referring expression features are selected...
...and multiplied element-wise with the mapped visual representations...
...to generate image-text similarity features.
These similarity features and visual features feed into the U-shape contextual attribute density estimator.
The estimator outputs a predicted attribute density map...
...which is supervised by the ground-truth contextual attribute density map...
...using an L2 density loss function during training.
Intermediate representations from the estimator form multi-scale CAD feature pyramids.
Next, the CAD Attention Module enhances visual features, starting with the Spatial Attention stage.
CAD features are provided at each scale.
Channel-wise two-dimensional max pooling...
...and average pooling are applied to compress channel information.
The pooled spatial features are concatenated...
...processed through a convolutional layer...
...and mapped through a sigmoid function to generate a spatial attention map.
The framework then enters the Channel Attention stage.
The original multi-scale visual features are received...
...and multiplied by the spatial attention map to highlight foreground areas.
Spatially attended features are pooled along the spatial dimensions using one-dimensional max pooling...
...and average pooling.
A shared multilayer perceptron processes the max-pooled channel vector...
...as well as the average-pooled channel vector.
The resulting vectors are summed together...
...and passed through a sigmoid function to produce the channel attention map.
Multiplying this map with the spatially attended features...
...yields the final CAD-enhanced visual features.
In parallel, the CAD Dynamic Query Module initializes decoder queries.
Under Density Initialization, CAD features are taken...
...and the top-K visual feature positions with highest similarity are selected.
Within the Text Initialization branch,
the text feature...
...undergoes a linear transformation...
...and GELU activation to produce dynamic text features.
The initial query embeddings...
...are multiplied by the dynamic text representations to compute text weight matrices.
Multiplying these weights with the original text feature creates text-dynamic queries.
A cross-attention module integrates the text-dynamic queries with the selected top-K CAD features...
...producing highly distinguishable dynamic queries.
The CAD-enhanced visual features and text features are gathered...
...and fed together with the dynamic queries into the Localization Decoder.
The decoder outputs precise bounding boxes and counting predictions matching the referring expression.
Training is finalized by optimizing the overall objective, combining the density loss and localization loss.
